payload.purpose_context: Part of the whole-pack round trip (epic #186, issue #195). The files that describe a pack as a whole - its activation presets, its Markdown description, its authored descriptor and its generated manifest - are loaded into the charter domain through deliberately designed, closed storage shapes and written back, so the whole-pack round-trip gate covers them and pack authors can rely on the service not to lose, invent or silently tolerate content at the pack level.
payload.purpose_tldr: Read every pack-level file of a Charter Pack (presets, pack.md, pack.yaml, pack-manifest.yaml) into the domain in a sanitized shape and write it back without loss of meaning.

payload.question: How far does the mission go with presets: round-trip as written, or the sanitized shape with the per-item must-have mark?

payload.final_answer: Sanitized shape with the per-item mark: schema_version, id (= file stem), description, activated_kinds, activated_<plural> and activated_mission_types lists of {id, must_have?} items; closed schema preset.schema.json.
payload.rationale: Operator requirement 2026-10-28 (sanitized DSOs) and the #195 ruling (a mark on each item). The as-written shape cannot carry the mark, so #206 would break the same files twice (squad F5). No contract surface carries presets (only @WIP journey prose).
payload.resolved_by: mission author (grounding squad); operator questions on #195

payload.question: How is a governing preset told from a convenience preset?

payload.final_answer: By its items: a preset with at least one must_have item governs; the required set is derived from the marks. No preset-level flag.
payload.rationale: Operator ruling on #195 (a mark on each item; one preset may hold both); one way to say a thing (S6); ADR-0031 decisions 1-2.
payload.resolved_by: mission author (grounding squad); operator questions on #195

payload.question: What happens to required_<plural> lists in this mission?

payload.final_answer: A preset never had them; the closed preset schema refuses any required_* key. Migrating org-charter.yaml's required_<plural> lists and refusing them there stays in #206.
payload.rationale: Operator ruling on #195: migrate then refuse, planned as its own mission after the epic.
payload.resolved_by: mission author (grounding squad); operator questions on #195

payload.question: How is an empty activation list in a preset treated?

payload.final_answer: Refused by the schema (minItems 1). A kind is switched off only by leaving it out of activated_kinds.
payload.rationale: Core reads [] as 'activate none' and absent as 'unrestricted', while ADR-0036 E2 makes them equal; refusing one spelling keeps both true without a comparator exception (squad F1, rule S6).
payload.resolved_by: mission author (grounding squad); operator questions on #195

payload.question: In what content form is pack.md held?

payload.final_answer: A pack-level payload of the bytes form (payloads rule */pack.md, kind pack-document); no schema.
payload.rationale: No frontmatter and no fields at the pin; bytes is built and the strictest equality; markdown and text stay unbuilt (ADR-0040).
payload.resolved_by: mission author (grounding squad); operator questions on #195

payload.final_answer: Close pack-descriptor.schema.json; remove PackDescriptor.undeclaredKeys and the PACK_UNKNOWN_KEY warning; an unknown key makes pack.yaml unreadable (PACK_UNREADABLE). contracts/charter/** is not edited; the stale pack_unknown_key description is raised on #195.
payload.rationale: ADR-0036 ruling 1 and decision 3 (accepted); the issue's 'keep the values' is superseded by refusal. No operation references the diagnostic; HTTP contract frozen unless the operator approves (squad F7).
payload.resolved_by: mission author (grounding squad); operator questions on #195

payload.final_answer: The authored-pack variant only: schema_version "1.0", manifest_hash, constituents [{kind, id, path, content_hash}], presets [{id, path, content_hash}]; closed. charter, fetched_at, source_url, source_type, generated_at, generated_by and provenance_path are not in it.
payload.rationale: Sanitized-shape rules S1-S5; the fetched and charter-bundle variants are not pack content (#110).
payload.resolved_by: mission author (grounding squad); operator questions on #195

payload.question: Is content_hash recomputed on write, or are constituents compared by bytes (ADR-0036 open question 3)?

payload.final_answer: Recomputed. content_hash and manifest_hash are derived: the writer recomputes them from the bytes it writes (content_hash = SHA-256 of LF-normalised bytes; manifest_hash = SHA-256 of RFC 8785 canonical JSON without manifest_hash). Membership is carried as read; a listed path missing from the written pack refuses the write. The reader does not check freshness; the gate verifies derived fields on both sides.
payload.rationale: Carrying hashes would describe bytes that no longer exist; comparing constituents by bytes contradicts ADR-0036 ruling 2 for YAML (squad F3, F9). JCS is emitter-independent.
payload.resolved_by: mission author (grounding squad); operator questions on #195

payload.question: What is the rule for kinds without a schema (ADR-0036 decision 6)?

payload.final_answer: Every file the round trip covers is a files rule with a closed schema (yaml), a payloads rule of a built non-yaml form, or an exclusion with a reason. A YAML file is never held without a schema. Derived fields are declared per kind in an ADR, never as a reader rule.
payload.rationale: Closes ADR-0036 open question 3 together with the manifest rule.
payload.resolved_by: mission author (grounding squad); operator questions on #195

payload.question: Does the verified-source fingerprint cover the pack-level files?

payload.final_answer: Yes: presets, pack.md and pack-manifest.yaml are appended to PackFileSet.digested after the templates.
payload.rationale: Every file the store reads is in the fingerprint (ADR-0040 decision 9 pattern); #110 stays the contract-scope decision about core's pin.
payload.resolved_by: mission author (grounding squad); operator questions on #195

payload.question: How are known-failure entries keyed before the open-packs issues exist?

payload.final_answer: spec-kitty/spec-kitty-open-packs#TBD-<slug>; the loader admits that form; the parent session files the issues, replaces the placeholders and may drop the TBD alternative before merge.
payload.rationale: Parent session instruction; the loader accepted only numeric keys (squad F6).
payload.resolved_by: mission author (grounding squad); operator questions on #195

payload.question: Parent-session coordination (2026-10-28): sibling #194 builds ADR-0040's markdown content form in its PR-A. Does pack.md stay a bytes payload?

payload.final_answer: No: pack.md consumes #194's markdown content form (supersedes the specify decision pack_md_form). The pack.md work package is sequenced last, depends on #194 PR-A merging, and rebases onto it; until then other:pack.md stays expected-red and only tests may stub the form. ADR number for this mission is 0043 (0041 #227, 0042 #194).
payload.rationale: Parent-session coordination message; one owner per content form (#194 builds markdown); avoids a second pack-level bytes kind.

payload.wp_title: Close pack.yaml: refuse unknown keys, retire undeclaredKeys
Manifest storage object, YAML format and hash recipes
Presets read, written, fingerprinted, validated and gated
Manifest owned by WholePackStore, regenerated on write, and gated
ADR-0043, amendment notes, changelog, glossary and architecture docs
Closed schemas for the preset and the pack manifest

payload.question: Operator answers on #195 (comment 6462447705, 2026-10-28) to the four questions of comment 6461881659

payload.final_answer: Q1 yes: designed preset shape with must_have now; built-in presets on the known-failure list. Q2 yes: edit DiagnosticCode.yaml so pack_unknown_key reads retired, never raised, plus a contract CHANGELOG line (no shape change). Q3 confirmed: authored-pack manifest, derived hashes on write, RFC 8785 manifest_hash; core first (C-1). Q4 agreed: restamp/membership stay with #110; no ULID pack_id pattern.

payload.question: Operator ruling on epic #186 (comment 6462455631, 2026-10-28): how does core figure in this mission?

payload.final_answer: It does not: operate as if core does not exist. No core-first sequencing, no core issue (draft C-1 dropped), no compatibility with core's current formats; built-in preset and manifest fixes are open-packs issues only, and seeding from core is open-packs' concern. Shapes and the RFC 8785 hash stand on their own merits. Supersedes the core-first parts of the specify decisions and of DM operator_answers_195 (Q3).
